subject: NVIDIA AVO applied to ARC-AGI-3 public set, August 21 2026
central_claim: NVIDIA's August 21, 2026 AVO report is a publishable AI engineering topic because the official NVIDIA technical blog, AVO paper, ARC-AGI-3 methodology and public ARC-AGI toolkit show a concrete shift in long-horizon agent evaluation from single model answers to a stateful execution loop with persistent memory, supervisor oversight, tools and environment feedback; the article treats reported scores as NVIDIA-run results, not independent performance verification.

selection.reason: The topic affects concrete engineering decisions for coding agents and long-running workflow agents: what to log, how to separate model capability from harness design, and how to evaluate memory, tools, feedback and supervisor policy. It has an official August 21 source, a technical paper, official benchmark methodology and public toolkit artifacts, supporting a bounded E2 center claim.

claims.claim: AVO shows a long-horizon agent system design in which persistent memory, supervisor oversight, tool use and execution feedback change the evaluation unit from a single model response to a stateful execution loop; reported ARC-AGI-3 and GPU-kernel results are NVIDIA-run claims rather than independent verification.

Opened the official OpenAI API changelog. The visible August 21, 2026 item records request-level regional processing for eligible API projects and a GPT-5.6 Sol update. It was useful for discovery but did not expose enough artifact-backed mechanism for an E2 center claim stronger than the selected AVO topic.
Opened Anthropic release-note paths. No August 21-22 model/API change with stronger novelty and E2 technical depth was found during this run.
Opened Gemini API changelog. Gemini 3.7 Flash GA remains a strong August 13 official model release, but it was already selected for the 2026-08-14 regular AI edition.

Reviewed Qwen blog/model registry paths and DeepSeek Hugging Face artifacts. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 has model card, config, weights and arXiv report, but DeepSeek V4-Pro/Harness was already covered by recent AI판 work and was not chosen for this regular slot.
Opened Mistral changelog and compared with the previous day's selected Mistral Agentic Search article. No newer Mistral release was found that should displace the selected AVO topic.

Opened xAI's August 21 Grok 4.6 on Google Enterprise Agent Platform post and Google's model documentation. The availability and quota details are concrete, but the center claim is mainly Preview distribution and product availability. It remained below the selected AVO topic on technical depth.

Opened NVIDIA's August 21 AVO technical blog. It describes the AVO agent loop, persistent memory, supervisor role, ARC-AGI-3 public-set setup, text-grid observation choice, 100.00 RHAE claim and caveats about uncontrolled comparison with VISTA.

Opened the AVO arXiv paper. It explains Agentic Variation Operators as autonomous coding agents replacing fixed evolutionary variation operators, with a seven-day NVIDIA Blackwell B200 attention-kernel optimization experiment. The paper is a method source but not an independent reproduction.

Opened ARC Prize's ARC-AGI-3 overview, scoring methodology, scorecard docs and llms.txt. These sources define interactive reasoning, RHAE scoring, scorecard handling and public toolkit routes used to bound the NVIDIA result.

Found the official ARC-AGI Toolkit GitHub and PyPI package paths. These artifacts support the article's claim that parts of the benchmark interface are public, while not implying that NVIDIA's AVO implementation or scorecard is public.

Search results and secondary summaries were used only to discover official paths across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, xAI, NVIDIA and ARC Prize. No article fact or score decision relies on search snippets or community posts without opened primary-source confirmation.

claim_source_ledger.claim: NVIDIA announced on August 21, 2026 that it applied AVO to ARC-AGI-3 public set and described AVO as a long-horizon agent architecture with persistent memory, supervision and tools.
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the official blog date, AVO description, architecture explanation and ARC-AGI-3 result section.
limitations: Confirms NVIDIA's announcement and self-described result.
Does not independently verify AVO performance or reproduce the run.
conflict_of_interest: NVIDIA authored the blog about its own research project.

claim_source_ledger.claim: The AVO paper defines Agentic Variation Operators as autonomous coding agents that replace fixed evolutionary variation operators by using lineage, domain knowledge and execution feedback to propose, repair, critique and verify edits.
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the abstract and method summary of the AVO paper.
limitations: The paper is authored by the AVO researchers and reports their experiments.
The AVO implementation was not confirmed as a public code artifact.
conflict_of_interest: Authors are affiliated with NVIDIA or collaborating institutions on the reported research.

claim_source_ledger.claim: ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive reasoning benchmark where agents explore unfamiliar environments, infer goals and rules through actions, and adapt over time.
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the official ARC-AGI-3 overview and benchmark description.
limitations: Benchmark design is described by its operator.
Public page does not itself verify NVIDIA's AVO score.
conflict_of_interest: ARC Prize Foundation operates the benchmark.

claim_source_ledger.claim: ARC-AGI-3 uses Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), combining completion and action efficiency against human baselines; 100% means completing all games and levels while matching or surpassing human efficiency.
claim_source_ledger.method: Read official scoring methodology and score interpretation sections.
limitations: Defines scoring method but does not provide NVIDIA's scorecard.
Human baseline sampling details are summarized, not independently audited.
conflict_of_interest: ARC Prize Foundation authors the scoring documentation.

claim_source_ledger.claim: NVIDIA reports that AVO completed the ARC-AGI-3 public set's 25 environments and 183 levels with a 100.00 RHAE score using 6,624 environment actions, while warning that comparison with VISTA is not a controlled ablation.
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the ARC-AGI-3 performance results and caveat paragraphs.
limitations: NVIDIA-run result, not an independent reproduction.
No public AVO scorecard ID, replay corpus or execution log was confirmed in this run.
Comparison with VISTA differs in agent backend, observation representation, memory and context management.
conflict_of_interest: NVIDIA reports the performance of its own research system.

claim_source_ledger.claim: ARC-AGI Toolkit is a public Python interface for ARC-AGI-3 environments that supports local and API interaction with benchmark environments.
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened official ARC Prize toolkit repository and corroborated with PyPI package page.
limitations: Toolkit public availability does not make the NVIDIA AVO harness public.
The toolkit was not installed or executed in this run.
conflict_of_interest: ARC Prize Foundation maintains the toolkit.

claim_source_ledger.claim: The PyPI arc-agi package is a public package for the ARC-AGI Toolkit.
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened PyPI package page discovered from official search and ARC docs.
limitations: Package metadata was not used to reproduce AVO.
Exact package version was not pinned in the article because the article does not provide installation instructions.
conflict_of_interest: Package is associated with ARC Prize toolkit maintainers.

reproducibility_detail.reason: The method, benchmark, scoring definition and public ARC toolkit are documented, but the AVO implementation, scorecard/replay logs and editor-run reproduction are unavailable or not executed.

No NVIDIA AVO code was cloned or run.
